sessions.title: Welcome
sessions.set_the_stage:
Welcome to Just Build. Over today you will go from never having built an agent to designing and watching a real one run, on a real problem. No coding background needed.

Here is the shape of the day: what an agent actually is, then the thinking behind a good one, then you do a real task by hand, design the agent for it, and watch it run.

Screens down and eyes up when we are talking; screens up when we are doing. Let's build.

sessions.title: Agents in the Real World: A Practitioner's View
sessions.set_the_stage:
We open with the practitioner's view. Before we touch any code, we answer the questions a working professional actually asks: what is an agent, where does it help, where does it fall down, and how do we keep it safe.

I'll walk you through these slides one idea at a time, with a wrong way and a right way for each. We'll slow down on the risks and on keeping a human in the loop; that is the grown-up part of this conversation.

By the end, you should be able to say in one sentence what an agent reads, decides, and produces, and name the one place it could quietly go wrong.

sessions.title: The Humanics of AI
sessions.set_the_stage:
This is the thinking layer, and it is where the real skill lives. The best agent-builders are not the fastest typists; they are the clearest thinkers. We'll work through first principles, systems thinking, decomposition, and how to define what good even means.

None of this is abstract. Every habit here points straight at the recruitment agent we build next. Breaking a task into atoms, seeing the whole pipe, and framing a sharp question are exactly what will make that agent easy to design.

Take these seriously and the build becomes the easy part. The clear thinking is what you'll carry into every agent you ever make.

sessions.title: Recruit by Hand
sessions.set_the_stage:
Before we build anything, you will do the recruitment job by hand. Here is your problem: 25 resumes and one job description, and time to interview only five people. Shortlist the best five yourselves.

This is where you learn what 'good' really looks like, and where your own judgement lives. Set your criteria before you read, score every resume on the same grid, and be able to say why each of your five made it.

The five you pick, with your reasons, become the yardstick we hold the agent to next. The cleaner your by-hand answer, the sharper the agent you design.

sessions.title: Design the Agentic Logic
sessions.set_the_stage:
Now we turn what you just did by hand into an agent, on paper, before any code. Box by box, we convert your own process into the agent's logic.

The facts you read become the extract. Your scoring grid becomes the code. The disqualifier you applied without even thinking becomes the hard rule. Your shortlist, with reasons, becomes a draft that a human approves.

When the design is right, the code is just typing it out. By the end you will have designed a complete agent, from your own hands, on a single page.

sessions.title: Watch It Being Built
sessions.set_the_stage:
You designed the recruitment agent on paper. Now watch it get built, live, on the exact 25 resumes you ranked by hand.

I open Make and build the whole thing in front of you, one module at a time. The read that pulls the facts from every resume. The score and the hard rule that decide who clears the bar. The router that splits shortlist from review. The draft that a human still has to approve.

Nothing is hidden and nothing is pre-baked. By the end you will have seen every step you do yourself tomorrow, and the agent's five will sit next to your five. That side by side is how you learn to trust it.

sessions.title: Summary of Day 1
sessions.set_the_stage:
Twenty-five resumes became a shortlist, in front of you, built from parts you could name. Before we close the day, we pull it together.

What the agent actually did, where the human stayed in the loop, and why the boring parts, the hard rule and the gate, are the parts that matter. This is the shape you carry into your own build tomorrow.

sessions.title: Pick Your Own
sessions.set_the_stage:
Yesterday the problem was ours: recruitment. Now you choose yours.

On the next screens is a palette of agents, one for every branch of engineering and every business function. Pick the one closest to a problem you actually care about. That choice is what you build tomorrow morning.

Same method as recruitment, pointed at your field. Choose well: you will spend two and a half hours with it.

sessions.title: Start Getting Ready to Build
sessions.set_the_stage:
You have picked your agent. Now we get you ready to build it, before you leave today.

You get the exact step by step guide for your use-case, the same kind you watched me follow for recruitment. We walk its shape together, you download the files you will need, and you confirm you can open everything.

Tonight is optional. If you want a head start, begin. If not, that is fine. The full build happens tomorrow with all of us in the room. Either way, you leave today knowing exactly what you are building and how.

sessions.title: Recheck Your Setup
sessions.set_the_stage:
Before you build, we make sure every account is ready, because a broken connection at 9am costs you the whole morning.

Google connections quietly expire overnight, so we reconnect them now, together. Open Make, confirm your scenario is there, reauthorize Google Drive and Google Sheets, and check your Recruitment Results sheet still has its two tabs.

Thirty minutes now saves an hour later. When your setup passes the checklist on screen, you are clear to build.

sessions.title: Build Your Own Agent
sessions.set_the_stage:
Yesterday you watched the recruitment agent get built. Today you build your own, start to finish, following the step by step guide for the use-case you picked.

Same shape as recruitment: read the document, score and apply the hard rule, route, then draft behind a human gate. You have the exact instructions, your setup is checked, and the facilitators are on the floor the whole time.

Work at your own pace. When you get stuck, wave one of us over. By the end of this session you will have a working agent on a problem from your own field, built with your own hands.

sessions.title: Operating Agents
sessions.set_the_stage:
You have built an agent. Now we cover the other half of the job: operating it. An agent that runs once in a workshop is easy; one that stays good for a year, on real data, in a changing world, is the real work.

We cover the ideas that keep an agent good in production: drift, why an agent is never done; evals, using your golden set as a living test; the harness that makes a flaky model dependable; context engineering; and how to watch, test and version a live agent. Build is a skill. Operate is a discipline.

sessions.title: Valuenomics: What's Your Agent Worth
sessions.set_the_stage: You built an agent and learned to operate it. Now: what is it worth? A working agent is not the prize; a measured, defensible outcome is. In this session we put a real number on your agent, using solid metrics for quality, efficiency and trust, bring them together on a dashboard, and add the governance that makes the value last: a named owner, an audit trail, and decisions you can defend. Value you can prove is value that pays.

sessions.title: Your Key Takeaways
sessions.set_the_stage:
The best part of the whole workshop: you teach the room. Every one of you takes the floor for two minutes and shares the three things that stuck.

First, ten quiet minutes to write your three, concrete and in your own words. Then each of you presents: your three takeaways, why they matter to you, and the one thing you will build or try next. Short and honest beats long and polished.

sessions.title: What Next
sessions.set_the_stage: Two days ago 'agent' was a buzzword; you leave able to build, operate and value one. In these last thirty minutes we look forward: what you now carry, how to keep building on it, the tools to keep playing with, how to stay current in a field that moves every month, and how to go deeper. Then we send you off to build.
